title: A good pure output has zero bad-event probability
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $T$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and let a learning program return a fixed value $a$ without random choices. If a predicate $P$ on its output space does not hold for $a$, then the probability that the output satisfies $P$ is zero.
